titleEn: Law on the Approval of the Agreement between the Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia and the People's Republic of China On the Promotion and Protection of Investment

articles.en:
Article 1. To approve the Agreement between the Royal Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investment, done at Phnom Penh on 19 July 1996, the full text of which is attached hereto.
Phnom Penh, [day illegible] [month illegible] 1999. Under the Royal Name and by Royal Command, respectfully submitted for the Royal signature. Signed, Hun Sen, Prime Minister. Respectfully submitted to Samdech the Prime Minister, Senior Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance, No. [illegible], signature, Keat Chhon. Agreement between the Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investment. 153
between the Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investment. The Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia and the Government of the People's Republic of China, hereinafter referred to as the "Contracting Parties".
Desiring to create favourable conditions for investment made by investors of one Contracting Party in the territory of the other Contracting Party.
[Illegible in source]
[Legacy-font text in source: not convertible to Unicode]
Desiring to intensify the economic cooperation of the two countries on the basis of equality and mutual benefit, the Contracting Parties have agreed as follows. 155
For the purposes of this Agreement:
1. The term "investment" means every kind of asset invested by investors of one Contracting Party in accordance with the laws and regulations of the other Contracting Party in the territory of the latter and shall in particular, though not exclusively, include the following assets: a. movable and immovable property as well as other rights in rem such as mortgages, pledges and other similar rights;
b. shares, stocks, debentures and any other form of participation in companies; c. claims to money or to any other performance having an economic and financial value; d. intellectual property rights, technical processes, know-how, trade marks and trade names;
e. business concessions conferred by law or under contract, including concessions to search for, cultivate, extract or exploit natural resources.
2. The term "investor" means: a. natural persons having the nationality of the Kingdom of Cambodia in accordance with its laws;
b. economic entities established in accordance with the laws of the Kingdom of Cambodia and having their seat in the territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia; c. natural persons having the nationality of the People's Republic of China in accordance with its laws;
d. economic entities established in accordance with the laws of the People's Republic of China and having their seat in the territory of the People's Republic of China.
3. The term "returns" means the amounts yielded by an investment, such as profits, dividends, interest, capital gains and any other lawful income.
4. The term "territory" means the territory of a Contracting Party as defined in its laws, including the maritime areas over which that Contracting Party has sovereignty, sovereign rights or jurisdiction in accordance with international law.
Article 2
1. Each Contracting Party shall encourage investors of the other Contracting Party to make investments in its territory and shall admit such investments in accordance with its laws and regulations.
2. Each Contracting Party shall, in accordance with its laws and regulations, give assistance and facilities, including the grant of visas and work permits, to nationals of the other Contracting Party engaged in activities connected with such investments in its territory.
Article 3
1. Investments and activities associated with investments made by investors of one Contracting Party shall be accorded fair and equitable treatment and shall enjoy protection in the territory of the other Contracting Party.
2. The treatment and protection referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall not be less favourable than that accorded to investments and activities associated with such investments of investors of a third State. The treatment and protection referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article shall not be less favourable than that accorded by a Contracting Party to investments of investors of any third State under a free trade area, customs union, economic union, an agreement for the avoidance of double taxation or an agreement for the facilitation of frontier trade.
[Illegible in source] Article 4
1. Neither Contracting Party shall take any measure of expropriation, nationalisation or any other measure having an equivalent effect (hereinafter referred to as "expropriation") against investments of investors of the other Contracting Party in its territory, except under the following conditions: a. for a public purpose;
b. in accordance with domestic legal procedure; c. without discrimination; d. against compensation.
2. The compensation referred to in paragraph 1(d) of this Article shall be equivalent to the value of the investment expropriated at the time when the expropriation was announced, and shall be freely convertible and transferable. Such compensation shall be paid without unreasonable delay. Article 5. Investors of one Contracting Party whose investments suffer losses owing to war, a state of emergency, insurrection, riot or other similar events in the territory of the other Contracting Party shall be accorded by the latter Contracting Party treatment, as regards restitution, indemnification and other settlement, not less favourable than that accorded to investors of a third State.
Article 6. 1. Each Contracting Party shall, subject to its laws and regulations, guarantee to investors of the other Contracting Party the transfer of their investments and returns held in its territory, including: a. profits, dividends, interest and other lawful income;
b. proceeds obtained from the total or partial liquidation of an investment; c. funds in repayment of loans related to an investment; [Legacy-font text in source: not convertible to Unicode]
3. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three arbitrators. Within six months from the date on which a Contracting Party received the written request for arbitration from the other Contracting Party, each Contracting Party shall appoint one arbitrator. Within the following two months, the two arbitrators so appointed shall, by mutual agreement of the two Contracting Parties, select a third arbitrator who is a national of a third State having diplomatic relations with both Contracting Parties. That third arbitrator shall be appointed by the two Contracting Parties as chairman of the arbitral tribunal.
4. If the arbitral tribunal has not been constituted within four months from the date of receipt of the written request for arbitration, and in the absence of any other agreement, each Contracting Party may invite the President of the International Court of Justice to appoint one or more arbitrators who have not yet been appointed. If the President is a national of either Contracting Party, or is prevented from performing the said function in relation to either Contracting Party, the member of the International Court of Justice next in seniority who is not a national of either Contracting Party shall be invited to make the appointment.
5. The arbitral tribunal shall determine its own procedure. The arbitral tribunal shall reach its decision by a majority of votes, in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement and the principles of international law recognised by both Contracting Parties. The decision shall be final and binding on both Contracting Parties. The arbitral tribunal shall, at the request of either Contracting Party, state the reasons for its decision.
7. Each Contracting Party shall bear the cost of its own arbitrator and of its representation in the arbitral proceedings,
and the cost of the chairman and the remaining costs shall be borne in equal parts by the two Contracting Parties.
d. additional payments under paragraph 1(d) of Article 1; e. payments for technical assistance or technical service fees and management fees; f. payments under a contract related to the project; g. earnings of nationals of the other Contracting Party who work in connection with the investment in the territory of the other Contracting Party.
2. The transfer referred to above shall be effected at the prevailing market rate of exchange of the Contracting Party receiving the investment on the date of transfer.
Article 7. If a Contracting Party or any of its agencies makes a payment to any of its investors under a guarantee it has given in respect of an investment in the territory of the other Contracting Party, the latter Contracting Party shall recognise the transfer of any right or claim of such investor to the former Contracting Party or its agency, and shall recognise the subrogation of the former Contracting Party or its agency to the rights and claims of such investor. The subrogated rights or claims shall not exceed the original rights or claims of such investor.

1. Any dispute between the Contracting Parties concerning the interpretation or application of this Agreement shall, as far as possible, be settled through diplomatic channels.
2. If the dispute cannot be settled through diplomatic channels within six months at the request of either Contracting Party, the dispute shall be submitted to an ad hoc arbitral tribunal for examination and decision.
Article 9
1. Any dispute arising between an investor of one Contracting Party and the other Contracting Party in connection with an investment in the territory of the latter Contracting Party shall be settled amicably through negotiations between the parties to the dispute.
2. If the dispute cannot be settled through negotiation within six months, either party to the dispute may submit it to the competent court of the Contracting Party which accepted the investment for decision.
3. If any dispute relating to the amount of compensation for expropriation cannot be settled within six months after recourse to negotiation as provided in paragraph 1 of this Article, the dispute may be submitted to an ad hoc arbitral tribunal for examination and decision at the request of either party. The provisions of this paragraph shall not apply if the investor concerned has submitted the dispute to the procedure provided in paragraph 2 of this Article.

6. The arbitral tribunal shall reach its decision by a majority of votes. The decision shall be final and binding on both disputing parties. The Contracting Parties undertake to implement the decision in accordance with their respective domestic laws.
7. The arbitral tribunal shall decide in accordance with the laws of the Contracting Party party to the dispute in which the investment is made, including its rules on conflict of laws, the provisions of this Agreement and the principles of international law generally recognised by both Contracting Parties.
8. Each Contracting Party shall bear the cost of its own arbitrator and of its appearance in the arbitral proceedings. The costs of the chairman and of the tribunal shall be borne in equal parts by the Contracting Parties.

1. This Agreement shall apply to investments made before or after its entry into force by investors of one Contracting Party in accordance with the laws and regulations of the other Contracting Party in the territory of the latter.

1. The representatives of the two Contracting Parties shall meet from time to time as necessary to: a. review the implementation of this Agreement; b. exchange information on legal and other matters relating to investment; c. [Illegible in source]
2. If either Contracting Party considers that any matter relating to investment so requires, the other Contracting Party shall promptly respond to the request for consultation and shall arrange the time and place therefor.

1. This Agreement shall enter into force on the first day of the following month after both Contracting Parties have notified each other in writing that their respective internal legal procedures have been completed. This Agreement shall remain in force for a period of [number illegible] years.
2. This Agreement shall continue in force unless one Contracting Party has given official notice to the other Contracting Party of its intention to terminate this Agreement within the period of one year as set out in paragraph 1 of this Article.
3. After the expiry of the initial period referred to above, either Contracting Party may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving at least one year's written notice to the other Contracting Party.
4. With respect to investments made prior to the termination of this Agreement, the provisions of Articles 1 to 12 shall continue in force for a further period of [number illegible] years from the date of termination.
In witness whereof, the undersigned, being duly authorised by their respective Governments, have signed this Agreement.
[Illegible in source] This document was executed in duplicate at Phnom Penh on 19 July 1996 in the Khmer, Chinese and English languages, all texts being equally authentic. In case of divergence of interpretation, the English text shall prevail.
For the Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia. For the Government of the People's Republic of China.
